sources.governing_condition_default_exception: create returns TreeID; move operations address the same target TreeID; delete hides a node and its children from visible state but children are not actually deleted; contains/nodes include deleted nodes and get_nodes can include them.

sources.observed_operation: Opened and inspected current conflict rules and examples; no code executed.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Concurrent writes to one property converge on a deterministic displayed winner while alternatives remain accessible through getConflicts; a later assignment resolves/hides the conflict. The order uses operation ID/counter and actor ID, not wall-clock time.
sources.applicability: Useful for retaining conflicting geometry/property values; the deterministic winner cannot decide human comment intent. The app must surface and record semantic resolution before a later write hides conflict data.

sources.locator: Map merge rules and list/RGA operation identity/order
sources.observed_operation: Opened algorithm reference and read map/list rules; no code executed.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: A map delete concurrent with a new value at the same key yields the new value; list operations address element IDs, not just numeric indices. Two same-position list inserts are ordered deterministically, but reverse insert patterns may not preserve intuitive order.
sources.applicability: Explicitly rules out assuming that a storage engine’s delete is delete-wins. Model explicit tombstone intent in the product layer and preserve order anchors; test simultaneous delete/edit.

sources.governing_condition_default_exception: A relative position is anchored to a sequence element and tracks insertions; it can be encoded/serialized. Absolute conversion returns null when the referenced position is unavailable or the shared type was deleted.
sources.applicability: Useful for comments on text/range-like sequences only. It is not a shape/connector identity and null resolution must leave the separate thread visible with original context.

sources.release_or_commit: main branch as served 2026-10-12; commit hash unavailable on rendered page
sources.locator: Yjs Internals > Deletions, Network protocol, Snapshots
sources.observed_operation: Opened upstream internals file and read deletion/GC/snapshot representation; no code executed.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Yjs records no who/when for a delete; with GC enabled deleted content is discarded and nested content may become a compact GC record. Sync updates carry insertions plus delete sets; snapshots pair state vectors with delete sets.
sources.applicability: Distinguishes engine tombstones from auditable product deletion events. If identity/author/reason/history is required, preserve that as application data; balance it against sensitive deleted content.

sources.observed_operation: Opened docs.rs StickyIndex API page and read its example and limits; no code executed.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: StickyIndex refers to a shared-sequence block and association side; it follows insertions, but an empty sequence yields no block ID and get_offset is a current-time index that can shift after later remote updates.
sources.applicability: Good for within-sequence/comment selection anchoring. It does not follow floor-plan geometry or prove that a visually similar replacement is the same entity.

sources.observed_operation: Opened the exact Rust API page and inspected defaults; no code executed.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Default text offsets use Bytes; skip_gc defaults false, so commit-time GC of deleted items is attempted unless skip_gc is enabled.
sources.applicability: Interop and anchor code must use the configured offset unit consistently; GC choice changes what deleted content can be recovered and must be evaluated with offline replicas and privacy/retention rules.
